# Unit A, phase 1: the new text's assertions, one per sentence

## 13. Error discipline
- V1 This chapter fixes how a failure is reported once it happens, and what the framework offers around it, taking as given what must be caught and where (§8.4) and when each fact is checked (§9). [§8.4, §9]
- V2 §13.1 covers the reporting policy; §13.2 the diagnostic representation; §13.3 the build primitives, `resolve` and the face-list accessors; §13.4 the runtime failure story; §13.5 the distinction between "the model reached a terminal state" and "the run should end"; §13.6 abnormal shutdown, one tail with two entries; §13.7 the tooling and component library that follow; and §13.8 the diagnosis of a rejected cycle. [§13.1, §13.2, §13.3, §13.4, §13.5, §13.6, §13.7, §13.8]
- V3 Two lessons FlightCore paid for ground this chapter.
- V4 The first is the compact-backtrace discipline, needed because parameterized model types make rendered output unreadable.
- V5 The second is the `SimulationTermination` machinery, which §13.5 replaces. [§13.5]

### 13.1 Reporting policy: collect the checks, fail the evaluations fast
- V6 The build's failure sites split into two populations.
- V7 That split settles the choice between fail-fast and compiler-style reporting.
- V8 Each population takes the policy that fits it.
- V9 This section covers, in order, the two populations and their policies, the step barrier, the dependency rule that decides which passes run past a failure, and the absence of cascade suppression.
- V10 Declarative checks over collected structure collect, and user-code evaluation fails fast (D-057). [D-057] (bold)
- V11 The collecting checks are those for unconnected inputs, two producers, wire typos and type mismatches, face-name uniqueness, `y_types`/state-field consistency and `sample_times` validation.
- V12 Each is a pass over a list.
- V13 The whole-tree obligation check literally computes the set of inputs whose obligation chain never terminates.
- V14 Reporting every violation is the natural output of such a pass, and truncating to the first would be extra work.
- V15 These failures also cluster in practice.
- V16 A freshly written assembly (pure composition, with no dynamics of its own) has five unwired inputs, and a renamed port breaks three wires.
- V17 Each of these passes returns its full violation list.
- V18 User code runs in the build's first three steps (§9.1). [§9.1]
- V19 The structure step reads the declaration bodies, interface-connection bodies among them.
- V20 The nominal evaluation runs every user function once, through the stage-1 probes (the build's single evaluations of a user function with real values) and the probe chain.
- V21 The activation at `T` runs the continuous tier's functions.
- V22 When user code throws, there is no meaningful rest of the collection to report.
- V23 A failed `input_wires` leaves the parent's face derivation undefined.
- V24 A failed stage-2 probe starves every downstream probe of its wired inputs, because probe values (the fabricated values a build-time probe runs on) flow topologically (§9.3). [§9.3]
- V25 The first user-code exception aborts the phase (D-057). [D-057]
- V26 The build's steps are barriers (D-259). [D-259]
- V27 A step that produced any error-severity diagnostic, from either population, throws before the next step begins.
- V28 Probing against unresolved wiring would be meaningless.
- V29 Collection reaches the step barrier, under a dependency rule (D-229). [D-229] (bold)
- V30 A declarative pass runs when the results it reads are clean.
- V31 It records every violation it finds and returns a total result.
- V32 Every pass that ran merges into the barrier's one throw.
- V33 Whether a pass can run past a failure follows from what it reads.
- V34 The structure step's walk yields two results, the component list and the wiring.
- V35 A wire that fails to resolve is recorded and claims nothing, so the obligation check reports its input as unfed.
- V36 Tier and event checking read only the component list, so they run and merge.
- V37 A structural failure leaves the subtree behind it unknown.
- V38 An unreadable or mixed class or a malformed container is such a failure.
- V39 No pass can read past it, so it throws alone.
- V40 In the two evaluating steps the probe chain consumes each check's subject as it goes.
- V41 A check that reads a failed probe does not run, so the chain's fail-fast follows from the same rule.
- V42 Outside the build the unit is the call.
- V43 Deployment validation (§9.2) runs every check whose premise holds and throws once. [§9.2]
- V44 The only partial results ever carried past a failure are violation lists and a claim table with the failed wires absent.
- V45 None of the three steps therefore needs machinery for carrying partial internal results across a failure.
- V46 That machinery was the cost that kept this decision open, and it never materializes.
- V47 There is no cascade suppression within a step (D-057). [D-057] (bold)
- V48 This is a deliberate simplification.
- V49 A wire typo'd as `:throtle` produces two errors.
- V50 One is a did-you-mean error (the offending name plus the list-in-hand it should have matched).
- V51 The other is an unconnected-input error for the intended `throttle`.
- V52 Both are reported in the one throw, and the did-you-mean names the input the other error says is unfed, so the pairing explains itself.

### 13.2 Diagnostics: structured values, one carrier exception
- V53 Both reporting policies move the same thing.
- V54 What a collecting pass returns and what a fail-fast site produces is in either case a diagnostic.
- V55 The shape of that value decides what an acceptance test can assert and what a user reads.

#### The diagnostic and its carrier
- V56 A diagnostic is a plain value from a small closed set of kinds (D-058). [D-058] (bold)
- V57 Appendix C enumerates that set normatively. [Appendix C]
- V58 For each kind it records the kind name, the payload fields, the owning section, the severity, where the kind is raised and under which policy (D-214). [D-214]
- V59 That index is the reference the §8.4 walkthroughs, run as acceptance tests, and the error-message work are written against. [§8.4]
- V60 Tests match on kind plus payload fields, never on message text, so messages are pure presentation (D-058). [D-058]
- V61 Each kind carries its own structured payload.
- V62 The payload holds endpoint paths, face names, expected and observed types, and the list-in-hand a did-you-mean needs (the offending name plus the list it should have matched).
- V63 A kind is a Julia type.
- V64 Severity is a property of the kind, not of the occurrence (D-214). [D-214] (bold)
- V65 It is `error` or `warning`, and it says whether an occurrence ever throws.
- V66 It is read as `severity(d)` and never stored per occurrence.
- V67 The severity field of Appendix C is derived from it. [Appendix C]
- V68 Where an occurrence surfaces (build, service or runtime) and how it is reported (collected, fail-fast, logged or rate-limited) are the raised and policy fields of Appendix C. [Appendix C]
- V69 Those two fields describe the occurrence, not the kind.
- V70 `BundleFieldError`, for example, is raised at the probe and as a `StepError` species (a `StepError` whose `cause` is a diagnostic) thereafter.
- V71 Checking passes return diagnostics.
- V72 The step barrier (each of the build's three steps throws before the next begins) throws a single `DiagnosticError` wrapping the collection.
- V73 A fail-fast site throws the same carrier exception holding one diagnostic.
- V74 The carrier's type parameter spells the policy (D-222). [D-222] (bold)
- V75 It is the diagnostic's kind for a fail-fast throw and `Vector{Diagnostic}` for a collected one.
- V76 A test therefore asserts policy and kind at once with `@test_throws DiagnosticError{Kind}`.
- V77 The runtime carrier follows the same rule with a parameter of its own, since `StepError{C}` carries the type of its `cause` (§13.4, D-225). [§13.4, D-225]
- V78 `showerror` renders a collection compiler-style, grouped by kind and sorted by path.
- V79 It renders a single diagnostic as its own line.
- V80 [code block] # a diagnostic value: its kind is its identity, its payload is plain data
- V81 Two rendering rules are doctrine, not style (D-058). [D-058]
- V82 The first is strings, never instances.
- V83 Diagnostics carry paths and names as strings, never component instances and never component types.
- V84 This is the lesson of FlightCore's `compact_backtrace`.
- V85 Expected and observed port types are the one payload exception, and they are small.
- V86 Examples are a `Float64` against a `Bool`, and a NamedTuple field diff.
- V87 The second is that the didactic style is policy.
- V88 Every diagnostic states the fix or the lists-in-hand, not just the violation.
- V89 Examples are "return `zero(x.ω)`, not `0`" and "no input `throtle`; did you mean `throttle`?", or the child's face list shown alongside the unknown name given to `except`.
- V90 A user-code exception is wrapped in a framing diagnostic, `UserCodeFraming`, with the original exception as `cause`.
- V91 The framing carries the component path, the function that threw, and the probe context, which is the bundle's field names (the bundle is the NamedTuple of zero-copy views a component function receives) and the synthesized inputs as a spelling, never as values (D-248). [D-248]
- V92 The didactic framing therefore renders first and the raw throw second.
- V93 The framed set is every user-authored method the build invokes (D-248). [D-248] (bold)
- V94 The declarations of §8.2 and the probed functions of §9.3 are framed alike, each reached through one framing accessor rather than a bare call. [§8.2, §9.3]
- V95 A declaration takes no bundle, so only the plain framing applies to it.
- V96 Three exceptions pass through the framing unwrapped, because none of them is user code failing.
- V97 They are a `DiagnosticError` carrier a check inside the call threw, an `InternalInvariant` (the exception a framework self-check raises, outside the kind set) (D-215), and an `InterruptException`. [D-215]
- V98 At runtime the same throw reaches the one runtime catch site (§13.4) instead. [§13.4]
- V99 There a `FieldError` matched as below becomes a `BundleFieldError` species, and any other exception rides as the `StepError`'s `cause`.
- V100 One exception type, the `FieldError`, is recognized rather than merely framed (D-341). [D-341] (bold)
- V101 A `FieldError` carries its type and field as data (Julia ≥ 1.12).
- V102 At the probe the framework matches them against the bundle's own NamedTuple type, which the accessor holds.
- V103 At the runtime catch site it matches them against the bundle's field names, because the bundle's type there is the activation's and is not in hand (D-248). [D-248]
- V104 A tuple the author builds with the bundle's own names is indistinguishable from the bundle at either site, and the diagnosis stays true of it.
- V105 The result is the bundle-law did-you-mean (§5.2). [§5.2]
- V106 It carries the legal field set and classifies the miss as an undeclared store, a wrong tier (the continuous or discrete side of the hybrid formalism), or a field illegal for this function.
- V107 Nothing is recovered by reading message text.
- V108 The probe raises the result as `BundleFieldError` (Appendix C, D-248). [Appendix C, D-248]
- V109 An example message is "`systems/plant`: `x_deriv` destructures `m`, but `systems/plant` declares no `m_init`".
- V110 The message names the component by its path.
- V111 One law covers tier facts, stage legality and declarations alike.
- V112 The wrong-tier miss covers the state letters too (D-195). [D-195]
- V113 `x` and `m` are continuous-only, and `s` and `Δt` are discrete-only, so destructuring any of the four on the wrong tier is a wrong-tier fact.
- V114 The bundle stays a bare NamedTuple (D-074, D-341). [D-074, D-341]
- V115 A getproperty-wrapper spelling is the recorded fallback, should type-matched interception prove insufficient (D-341). [D-341]

#### Where warnings live
- V116 A warning raised while producing an artifact lives on that artifact (D-250). [D-250] (bold)
- V117 A warning raised while mutating state lives in that state's status.
- V118 Logging is presentation and never a home.
- V119 An artifact is an immutable pure function of its inputs.
- V120 State is single-owner and mutated in place.
- V121 That one criterion places every warning the framework raises.
- V122 The build produces artifacts, so its warnings live on them.
- V123 §9.2 states which artifacts carry them, how `warnings(x)` reads the list, and how a step that throws or completes presents them. [§9.2]
- V124 The build's warning set holds `EmptyFaceSelection` (§8.8, D-251). [§8.8, D-251]
- V125 The warning set of the `Deployment` (the scalar-free artifact the grid parameters fix) holds `GridUtilization` (D-254). [D-254]
- V126 The unconnected-output warning stays rejected (§6.1, D-084), so the collected-warning slot stays open and empty. [§6.1, D-084]
- V127 A warnings-as-errors switch is rejected, since a warning is a fact about the model, not a defect (D-250). [D-250]
- V128 A stopped-sim service returns an artifact, so its warnings live on it.
- V129 `trim!` returns a `TrimReport`, and `TrimCommitEvents`, `TrimCommitResiduals` and `TrimCommitChecks` are that report's fields (§14.8). [§14.8]
- V130 The line the call prints at return is presentation.
- V131 `attach!` is the other side of the criterion.
- V132 It mutates the roster (the list of attached device entries).
- V133 `EmptyGreedyClaim` therefore lands in the roster entry's diagnostic cell (the single-writer cell each writer owns for diagnostics and heartbeat) (§11.6, D-250). [§11.6, D-250]
- V134 The runtime mutates state, so its warnings live in that state's status.
- V135 The stream is per-occurrence.
- V136 The per-writer diagnostic cells carry it (§11.8, D-136). [§11.8, D-136]
- V137 The rate limit lives in the cells, as a structural bound rather than a policy layered over the stream.
- V138 The bound is a bounded ring plus per-kind suppressed counts, drained at frame top.
- V139 So "rate-limited wherever its source can repeat" holds of every kind below without any kind arranging it.
- V140 The stream surfaces through the published framework status (§11.2). [§11.2]
- V141 The liveness heartbeat (§12.2) rides in the same cells, and the pacer's record (§10.7) sits beside the writers' records in the status. [§12.2, §10.7]
- V142 The stream is never collected, since there is no collection to join.
- V143 Nothing in the argument of D-084 applies to it. [D-084]
- V144 That decision is about what the build warns on.
- V145 The committed runtime warnings, in one place, are these.
- V146 `ChatteringBudget`, chattering or localization-budget exhaustion (§10.4). [§10.4]
- V147 A localized event's bracketing budget runs out at a boundary (a published consistency point).
- V148 `FiringBudget`, firing-budget exhaustion (§10.6). [§10.6]
- V149 An event has spent its `firing_budget` at a boundary, and its further edges there are dropped.
- V150 `DebtReanchor`, a forgiven-debt re-anchor (§10.7). [§10.7]
- V151 The pacer abandons its accumulated debt and re-anchors its schedule.
- V152 The write-surface and batch-entry violations (§11.3, §11.4), all raised at staging. [§11.3, §11.4]
- V153 The drain checks nothing.
- V154 `OutOfClaimEntry` is an enumerated surface's binding drift, a name with no position in the attach-compiled schema.
- V155 `ClaimedFaceEntry` is a harness write to a face claimed in the run's frozen partition, and it names the incumbent.
- V156 The stopped-sim attach also fires it when it renormalizes a pending batch.
- V157 `EntryTypeMismatch` is a value unconvertible to its root input's declared type, rejected at staging for every writer.
- V158 `MalformedDatum`, a tolerated device-side datum failure (§11.6, §13.4). [§11.6, §13.4]
- V159 It is emitted by the author's loop via `report!(handle, …)` into the device's own cell (§11.8, D-105). [§11.8, D-105]
- V160 It replaces FlightCore's `InputMappingError`.
- V161 `ReplayDiscardedStaging`, staging discarded during replay (§12.7). [§12.7]
- V162 It reports a live batch found staged while the trace feeds the drain.
- V163 `ThreadBudget`, thread-budget tightness (§12.2). [§12.2]
- V164 It is raised once per run, at `run!` or `replay!`, against the frozen roster (D-401). [D-401]
- V165 `DeviceJoinTimeout`, a device join timeout (§12.4). [§12.4]
- V166 A device task exceeds the shutdown join timeout and is abandoned by name rather than hanging `run!`.
- V167 It arises after the terminal snapshot.
- V168 It is therefore collected into the termination record and presented through the logging backend, never carried into a status (D-201, D-203). [D-201, D-203]
- V169 `DeviceCrash`, a device crash (§12.4, §13.4). [§12.4, §13.4]
- V170 A genuine bug takes the per-device crash path.
- V171 The framework wrapper catches a device task's failure and reports `DeviceCrash`, and the run goes on without the device unless its attachment set `should_abort` (§11.6). [§11.6]
- V172 `UnboundedRun`, an unbounded run (§13.5). [§13.5]
- V173 It lands in the loop's own cell, because `run!` mutates state (D-255). [D-255]
